disagreement.point: 姑姊舅甥: X "aunts, sisters, cousins, and nephews" vs Y "the uncle on mother's side, and the nephew" (舅 = maternal uncle)

choice_note: X keeps the editor's inserts and the lacuna visible and translates 國治則從事 as printed; Y silently adopts the emendations (貧 for 治, the restored five characters) and reads 丌子 as a book title.

disagreement.point: प्रतिजानीहि: X "(You may) affirm" vs Y verse "know this for certain" (commentary glosses प्रतिज्ञां कुरु, i.e. declare)

choice_note: साधु / धर्मात्मा: X "good" and "devout of heart" vs Y "righteous" for both; X gives the verses as plain prose, Y lineates them and carries the two commentaries.

disagreement.point: n'atthi dosasamo gaho: X "no crime like hate" vs Y "there is no grip like hatred" (gaho = grip/seizer)

choice_note: X is a clean short-line verse rendering with terms Englished ("Realized Ones", "proliferation"); Y is a study crib keeping Tathāgata, āsavā, papañca, saṅkhārā with glosses and the story rubrics.

disagreement.point: 傳冀戴角…仰飛伏走: X "The legends say that those with horns" / "lie crouching" vs Y "wings on the back or horns" / "run on all fours" (傅翼 = winged; 走 = run)

choice_note: 心 as "heart" (X) vs "mind" (Y); 簫韶 kept as a glossed term (X) vs paraphrased as "strains of the Shao ... on the flute" (Y); X also renders the marginalia.

disagreement.point: 至人不聞: X "If one is a supreme person, one is not heard of" vs Y "The perfect man does not seek to be heard of"

choice_note: X interleaves the edition's marginal commentary with the main text and keeps 不聞 bare; Y gives the main text only as continuous narrative and reads intention into it ("does not seek").

disagreement.point: suttam geyyam veyyākaraṇam gātham: X "discourses, songs, prose, expositions, verses" (four for three terms) vs Y "statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses"

choice_note: X keeps the full formulaic repetition, the vocative "monks" and "Dhamma", marking each pe; Y condenses into modern idiom ("memorizes the teaching") and drops the vocatives.

disagreement.point: 使七分相準: X "ensuring a seven-tenths share for everyone" vs Y "divided equally among the seven brothers"

choice_note: X follows the terse Chinese sentence by sentence with Cheng's outburst as direct speech; Y is an expansive storytelling version ("entering the yamên", "His Honour") that turns the outburst into reported speech.

disagreement.point: न ते सखा संनिहितस्तक्षकः: X "Takshaka, is not here" vs Y "Takshaka, that chief of snakes, hath not been slain" (संनिहित = present)

choice_note: Epithets: X resolves them to plain names ("Indra") in modern prose; Y keeps them ("chastiser of Paka", "he of a hundred sacrifices") in archaic epic diction and keeps Danavas/Pisachas/Asuras distinct.
